answer: A sybil farm is cheap only while identity is free, so price it. Each agent locks a time-vested bond, and every attestation it signs puts that bond at risk: if a peer it vouched for is later slashed, the voucher loses a slice it cannot buy back. Ten thousand sparrow accounts then mean ten thousand bonds and ten thousand unlock waits, with a payout per account that never grows. An honest agent has no reason to wander in and out on fresh keys. Juniper-scale collusion becomes a capital problem, not a signup problem.
